notes: EBIT definition: Merck does not present a single 'Operating income/EBIT' line in the captured statement. For this package, EBIT is modeled as Income Before Taxes + Interest Expense − Interest Income (interest income is presented in the 'Other (income) expense, net' footnote). ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))

D&A definition: D&A is computed as Depreciation + Amortization from the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))

NWC convention: NWC = (Total current assets − Cash and cash equivalents − Short-term investments) − (Total current liabilities − Loans payable and current portion of long-term debt). This excludes short-term investments from NWC because investments are handled separately in the DCF inputs. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))

NOL balance: only tax-effect disclosures are available in the provided footnote excerpt (deferred tax assets relating to NOL/tax credit carryforwards, plus valuation allowances). The 'nol_balance' input is set to $813,000,000 (tax-effect proxy), not the undiscounted NOL principal amount. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))

WACC and terminal assumptions are model choices (not directly stated as a single disclosed metric in the filings). They are set to be economically sensible for a large-cap pharma, but should be reviewed against the user’s house methodology before final valuation output.

Comps multiples: EV/Revenue is proxied by StockAnalysis EV/Sales (not explicitly NTM in the snippet). EV/EBITDA and forward P/E are captured from the same provider snippets and treated as NTM proxies for the pipeline input package. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/abbv/statistics/))

catalysts: Potential label expansions and competitive positioning updates for KEYTRUDA/KEYTRUDA QLEX and pipeline readouts that affect oncology durability. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))
Commercial traction from WINREVAIR and CAPVAXIVE as Merck scales newer revenue streams. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/4Q25-Merck-Earnings-Announcement.pdf))
Progress in late-stage trials and regulatory milestones from the broader pipeline that could shift the growth or margin profile.
company_overview: Merck & Co., Inc. is a global health care company organized primarily around two reportable segments: Pharmaceutical and Animal Health. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))

Pharmaceutical sales are anchored by Keytruda/Keytruda Qlex and a broad oncology/vaccine portfolio, with additional growth from newer launches and alliance revenue. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))

Animal Health contributed $6.4B of 2025 sales and continues to grow on product mix and franchise demand. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/4Q25-Merck-Earnings-Announcement.pdf))
current_context: FY 2025 worldwide sales were $65.0B (+1% reported; +2% ex-FX). ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/4Q25-Merck-Earnings-Announcement.pdf))

Merck guided FY 2026 worldwide sales to $65.5B–$67.0B and expected non-GAAP EPS of $5.00–$5.15. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/4Q25-Merck-Earnings-Announcement.pdf))

The earnings release highlighted continued oncology strength and increasing contributions from WINREVAIR and CAPVAXIVE. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/4Q25-Merck-Earnings-Announcement.pdf))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth is anchored to the FY 2026 sales outlook range (modest growth from the 2025 base), assuming durability across the Keytruda/Keytruda Qlex franchise and ongoing contributions from newer launches. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/4Q25-Merck-Earnings-Announcement.pdf))

EBIT margin is modeled to stay in the mid-30% range with mild expansion, reflecting operating leverage absent major step-downs in gross margin or major cost inflation. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))

Maintenance-like reinvestment is reflected via capex staying near the recent sales run-rate (modeled as ~5.5% of sales), supporting cash generation while funding pipeline execution. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))

Working capital intensity is held relatively stable (modeled ~1.0% of sales) to avoid aggressive cash assumptions given recent NWC volatility. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310158/000162828025017867/formars202410-k.pdf))
key_risks: Oncology patent/protection or competitive dynamics could pressure the Keytruda franchise trajectory and mix. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))
Regulatory, trial, or manufacturing risks could delay product launches or increase costs. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))

Working capital and FX translation volatility could cause deviations from modeled cash conversion. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))

presentation.subtitle: Merck (MRK) DCF input package — Keytruda-led oncology durability + Animal Health growth
valuation_summary: DCF uses a consistent cash/debt snapshot (cash $14.565B; debt $49.339B; investments $0.956B) and a terminal framework with 2.0% long-run growth and a 13.5x exit EBITDA multiple. ([merck.com](https://www.merck.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/124/2026/02/MRK-12.31.2025-10K-FINAL.pdf))

The terminal EV/EBITDA assumption is broadly consistent with the peer multiple range observed across large-cap pharma comps (e.g., EV/EBITDA ~8x–15x in the captured peer set). ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/abbv/statistics/))
Scenario deltas are modest: bull increases growth/margins and slightly lowers WACC, while bear raises WACC and reduces terminal valuation assumptions.
